evidence: Computational prediction by lncLocator shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B indicates ribosomal localization.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 bound with RPS3.
source: Our RNA pulldown (RPD) assay also proved that VPS9D1-AS1 bound with RPS3, one of the proteins constituting the small ribosomal subunit (Figure 3K).
evidence: RNA pulldown assay in Figure 3K shows RPS3 protein binding to VPS9D1-AS1 probes.

claim: RPS3 is one of the proteins constituting the small ribosomal subunit.
source: Our RNA pulldown (RPD) assay also proved that VPS9D1-AS1 bound with RPS3, one of the proteins constituting the small ribosomal subunit (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about RPS3.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression prevented RPS3 degradation caused by CX5461 treatment.
source: We found that VPS9D1-AS1 OE prevented RPS3 degradation caused by CX5461 (an inhibitor of RNA polymerase I transcription of ribosomal RNA genes) treatment.
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 3L shows maintained RPS3 levels in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells after CX5461 treatment.

claim: CX5461 is an inhibitor of RNA polymerase I transcription of ribosomal RNA genes.
source: We found that VPS9D1-AS1 OE prevented RPS3 degradation caused by CX5461 (an inhibitor of RNA polymerase I transcription of ribosomal RNA genes) treatment.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about CX5461 function.

claim: CX5461 treatment immediately increased the levels of TGF-β, which declined over time.
source: However, CX5461 treatment immediately increased the levels of TGF-β, which declined over time.
evidence: Western blotting time course in Figure 3L shows initial increase then decrease in TGF-β after CX5461 treatment.

claim: In VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cells, the levels of TGFBR1 were decreased after treatment with CX5461.
source: In VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells, the levels of TGFBR1 and SMAD1/5/9 were decreased after treatment with CX5461, but the TGF-β levels did not decrease following the degradation of RPS3 (Figure 3L).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 3L shows decreased TGFBR1 in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells after CX5461 treatment.

claim: In VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cells, the levels of SMAD1/5/9 were decreased after treatment with CX5461.
source: In VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells, the levels of TGFBR1 and SMAD1/5/9 were decreased after treatment with CX5461, but the TGF-β levels did not decrease following the degradation of RPS3 (Figure 3L).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 3L shows decreased SMAD1/5/9 in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells after CX5461 treatment.

claim: In VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cells, TGF-β levels did not decrease following the degradation of RPS3 after CX5461 treatment.
source: In VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells, the levels of TGFBR1 and SMAD1/5/9 were decreased after treatment with CX5461, but the TGF-β levels did not decrease following the degradation of RPS3 (Figure 3L).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 3L shows maintained TGF-β levels in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells despite RPS3 degradation.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 scaffolds the TGF-β protein and regulates its translation in ribosomes.
source: These findings suggest that VPS9D1-AS1 scaffolds the TGF-β protein and regulates its translation in ribosomes.
evidence: The binding of VPS9D1-AS1 to RPS3 and TGF-β, and the effects of ribosome inhibition support this conclusion.

claim: A total of 705 differentially expressed genes were identified between HCT116 sgControl and sgVPS cells, including 203 upregulated genes and 502 downregulated genes.
source: A total of 705 differentially expressed genes were identified, which included 203 upregulated genes and 502 downregulated genes (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A identifies differentially expressed genes.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 knockout significantly inactivated IFNα/β signaling.
source: VPS9D1-AS1 KO significantly inactivated IFNα/β signaling and the cell death pathway as well as immune system processes (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C).
evidence: Gene ontology and GSEA analyses in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C show inactivation of IFNα/β signaling.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 knockout significantly inactivated the cell death pathway.
source: VPS9D1-AS1 KO significantly inactivated IFNα/β signaling and the cell death pathway as well as immune system processes (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C).
evidence: GSEA in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C shows inactivation of cell death pathways.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 knockout significantly inactivated immune system processes.
source: VPS9D1-AS1 KO significantly inactivated IFNα/β signaling and the cell death pathway as well as immune system processes (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C).
evidence: GSEA in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C shows inactivation of immune system processes.

claim: IFI27 was one of the most significantly downregulated genes upon VPS9D1-AS1 knockout.
source: IFI27 and OAS1 were the most significantly downregulated genes upon VPS9D1-AS1 KO (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: qRT-PCR validation in Figure 4C shows significant downregulation of IFI27 in VPS9D1-AS1 KO cells.

claim: OAS1 was one of the most significantly downregulated genes upon VPS9D1-AS1 knockout.
source: IFI27 and OAS1 were the most significantly downregulated genes upon VPS9D1-AS1 KO (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: qRT-PCR validation in Figure 4C shows significant downregulation of OAS1 in VPS9D1-AS1 KO cells.

claim: OAS1 was significantly overexpressed in CRC cancer tissues according to TCGA datasets.
source: Analyses in TCGA datasets demonstrated that OAS1 and IFI27 were significantly overexpressed in CRC cancer tissues (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: TCGA analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E shows higher OAS1 expression in cancer tissues.

claim: IFI27 was significantly overexpressed in CRC cancer tissues according to TCGA datasets.
source: Analyses in TCGA datasets demonstrated that OAS1 and IFI27 were significantly overexpressed in CRC cancer tissues (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: TCGA analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E shows higher IFI27 expression in cancer tissues.

claim: The levels of OAS1 were significantly related to VPS9D1-AS1 levels in CRC tissue samples.
source: Pearson correlation analysis revealed that the levels of OAS1, but not IFI27, were significantly related to VPS9D1-AS1 levels (Figure 4E).
evidence: Pearson correlation in Figure 4E shows significant positive correlation between OAS1 and VPS9D1-AS1.

claim: The levels of IFI27 were not significantly related to VPS9D1-AS1 levels in CRC tissue samples.
source: Pearson correlation analysis revealed that the levels of OAS1, but not IFI27, were significantly related to VPS9D1-AS1 levels (Figure 4E).
evidence: Pearson correlation in Figure 4E shows no significant correlation between IFI27 and VPS9D1-AS1.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 knockout resulted in the downregulation of STAT1 after hIFNα stimulation.
source: After hIFNα stimulation, we found that VPS9D1-AS1 KO resulted in the downregulation of STAT1 and pSTAT1 (Figure 4F).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4F shows decreased STAT1 in VPS9D1-AS1 KO cells after IFNα treatment.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 knockout resulted in the downregulation of pSTAT1 after hIFNα stimulation.
source: After hIFNα stimulation, we found that VPS9D1-AS1 KO resulted in the downregulation of STAT1 and pSTAT1 (Figure 4F).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4F shows decreased pSTAT1 in VPS9D1-AS1 KO cells after IFNα treatment.

claim: hTGF-β treatment inhibited the phosphorylation of STAT1 induced by hIFNα stimulation.
source: When the cells were treated with hTGF-β, the phosphorylation of STAT1 induced by hIFNα stimulation was inhibited (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F shows reduced pSTAT1 when cells are treated with both hTGF-β and hIFNα.

claim: Blocking TGF-β signaling by siRNA-mediated knockdown of TGF-β reduced OAS1 expression.
source: We further performed siRNA-mediated KD of TGF-β, TGFBR1, and SMAD1 and confirmed that blocking TGF-β signaling reduced OAS1 and IFI27 expression (Figure 4G).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4G shows decreased OAS1 after TGF-β knockdown.

claim: Blocking TGF-β signaling by siRNA-mediated knockdown of TGFBR1 reduced OAS1 expression.
source: We further performed siRNA-mediated KD of TGF-β, TGFBR1, and SMAD1 and confirmed that blocking TGF-β signaling reduced OAS1 and IFI27 expression (Figure 4G).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4G shows decreased OAS1 after TGFBR1 knockdown.

claim: Blocking TGF-β signaling by siRNA-mediated knockdown of SMAD1 reduced OAS1 expression.
source: We further performed siRNA-mediated KD of TGF-β, TGFBR1, and SMAD1 and confirmed that blocking TGF-β signaling reduced OAS1 and IFI27 expression (Figure 4G).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4G shows decreased OAS1 after SMAD1 knockdown.

claim: Blocking TGF-β signaling by siRNA-mediated knockdown of TGF-β reduced IFI27 expression.
source: We further performed siRNA-mediated KD of TGF-β, TGFBR1, and SMAD1 and confirmed that blocking TGF-β signaling reduced OAS1 and IFI27 expression (Figure 4G).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4G shows decreased IFI27 after TGF-β knockdown.

claim: Blocking TGF-β signaling by siRNA-mediated knockdown of TGFBR1 reduced IFI27 expression.
source: We further performed siRNA-mediated KD of TGF-β, TGFBR1, and SMAD1 and confirmed that blocking TGF-β signaling reduced OAS1 and IFI27 expression (Figure 4G).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4G shows decreased IFI27 after TGFBR1 knockdown.

claim: Blocking TGF-β signaling by siRNA-mediated knockdown of SMAD1 reduced IFI27 expression.
source: We further performed siRNA-mediated KD of TGF-β, TGFBR1, and SMAD1 and confirmed that blocking TGF-β signaling reduced OAS1 and IFI27 expression (Figure 4G).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4G shows decreased IFI27 after SMAD1 knockdown.

claim: The expression levels of OAS1 were more significantly affected than IFI27 by blocking TGF-β signaling.
source: The expression levels of OAS1 were more significantly affected than IFI27 (Figure 4G).
evidence: Comparison of fold changes in Figure 4G shows greater reduction in OAS1 than IFI27.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression restored OAS1 expression after TGF-β signaling blockade.
source: In contrast, VPS9D1-AS1 OE restored OAS1 and IFI27 expression (Figure 4G).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4G shows increased OAS1 in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells after TGF-β pathway knockdown.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression restored IFI27 expression after TGF-β signaling blockade.
source: In contrast, VPS9D1-AS1 OE restored OAS1 and IFI27 expression (Figure 4G).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4G shows increased IFI27 in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells after TGF-β pathway knockdown.

claim: OAS1 and IFI27 mRNA levels were significantly reduced in VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cells.
source: Surprisingly, OAS1 and IFI27 mRNA levels were significantly reduced in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells, although VPS9D1-AS1 was stably upregulated by ~180.40 times in HCT116 cells and ~42.28 times in SW480 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G-H).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H shows decreased OAS1 and IFI27 mRNA in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: hIFNα stimulation significantly increased OAS1 in VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cells.
source: However, hIFNα stimulation significantly increased OAS1 and IFI27 in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells (Figure 4H-I).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4H shows increased OAS1 protein after IFNα treatment in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: hIFNα stimulation significantly increased IFI27 in VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cells.
source: However, hIFNα stimulation significantly increased OAS1 and IFI27 in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells (Figure 4H-I).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 4I shows increased IFI27 protein after IFNα treatment in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: SMAD4 antibodies immunoprecipitated the promoter regions of the OAS1 gene.
source: We confirmed that SMAD4 antibodies immunoprecipitated the promoter regions of both the OAS1 (–77 to +284) and IFI27 (–1933 to –1843) genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: ChIP assay in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I shows enrichment of OAS1 promoter with SMAD4 antibody.

claim: SMAD4 antibodies immunoprecipitated the promoter regions of the IFI27 gene.
source: We confirmed that SMAD4 antibodies immunoprecipitated the promoter regions of both the OAS1 (–77 to +284) and IFI27 (–1933 to –1843) genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: ChIP assay in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I shows enrichment of IFI27 promoter with SMAD4 antibody.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression significantly enhanced the binding between SMAD4 and the promoter regions of OAS1.
source: Importantly, VPS9D1-AS1 OE significantly enhanced the binding between SMAD4 and the promoter regions of OAS1 but failed to enhance this binding in the IFI27 promoter region (Figure 4J).
evidence: ChIP assay in Figure 4J shows increased SMAD4 binding to OAS1 promoter in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression failed to enhance the binding between SMAD4 and the IFI27 promoter region.
source: Importantly, VPS9D1-AS1 OE significantly enhanced the binding between SMAD4 and the promoter regions of OAS1 but failed to enhance this binding in the IFI27 promoter region (Figure 4J).
evidence: ChIP assay in Figure 4J shows no significant change in SMAD4 binding to IFI27 promoter in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: The levels of OAS1 were consistently elevated in CRC tissue samples that had positive VPS9D1-AS1 expression.
source: Moreover, IHC analysis indicated that the levels of OAS1, IFNAR1, and TGFBR1 were consistently elevated in CRC tissue samples that had positive VPS9D1-AS1 expression (Figure 4K~L).
evidence: IHC analysis in Figure 4L shows higher OAS1 levels in VPS9D1-AS1 positive tissues.

claim: The levels of IFNAR1 were consistently elevated in CRC tissue samples that had positive VPS9D1-AS1 expression.
source: Moreover, IHC analysis indicated that the levels of OAS1, IFNAR1, and TGFBR1 were consistently elevated in CRC tissue samples that had positive VPS9D1-AS1 expression (Figure 4K~L).
evidence: IHC analysis in Figure 4L shows higher IFNAR1 levels in VPS9D1-AS1 positive tissues.

claim: The levels of TGFBR1 were consistently elevated in CRC tissue samples that had positive VPS9D1-AS1 expression.
source: Moreover, IHC analysis indicated that the levels of OAS1, IFNAR1, and TGFBR1 were consistently elevated in CRC tissue samples that had positive VPS9D1-AS1 expression (Figure 4K~L).
evidence: IHC analysis in Figure 4L shows higher TGFBR1 levels in VPS9D1-AS1 positive tissues.

claim: OAS1 involved in IFN signaling acts downstream of TGF-β signaling and is increased by VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression.
source: Collectively, OAS1 involved in IFN signaling acts downstream of TGF-β signaling and increased by VPS9D1-AS1 OE.
evidence: The data showing OAS1 regulation by TGF-β pathway components and VPS9D1-AS1, plus SMAD4 binding to OAS1 promoter, support this conclusion.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 knockout reduced the expression of IFNAR1 on the surface of HCT116 cells.
source: When we examined the changes in IFNAR1 on the surface of HCT116 cells by flow cytometry (FCM), we found that VPS9D1-AS1 KO reduced the expression of IFNAR1 (Figure 5A).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 5A shows decreased IFNAR1 surface expression in VPS9D1-AS1 KO cells.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression significantly upregulated the expression of IFNAR1 in tumor cells.
source: Conversely, VPS9D1-AS1 OE significantly upregulated the expression of IFNAR1 in tumor cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 5B shows increased IFNAR1 surface expression in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: The deletion of OAS1 decreased the expression of IFNAR1.
source: Our results demonstrated that the deletion of OAS1 decreased the expression of IFNAR1, although VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells were resistant to this effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 5B shows decreased IFNAR1 in OAS1 knockout cells.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cells were resistant to the effect of OAS1 deletion on IFNAR1 expression.
source: Our results demonstrated that the deletion of OAS1 decreased the expression of IFNAR1, although VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells were resistant to this effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 5B shows maintained IFNAR1 levels in VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells even after OAS1 knockout.

claim: The deletion of OAS1 inhibited STAT1 expression.
source: In addition, the deletion of OAS1 inhibited STAT1 and TGF-β expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A shows decreased STAT1 in OAS1 knockout cells.

claim: The deletion of OAS1 inhibited TGF-β expression.
source: In addition, the deletion of OAS1 inhibited STAT1 and TGF-β expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A shows decreased TGF-β in OAS1 knockout cells.

claim: Coculture with VPS9D1-AS1 knockout cells increased IFNAR1 expression in CD8+ T cells.
source: In vitro-primed T cells were cultured with HCT116 sgControl and sgVPS cell lines. Coculture with VPS9D1-AS1 KO cells increased IFNAR1 expression in CD8+ and CD4+ T cells (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 5C shows increased IFNAR1 on CD8+ T cells cocultured with VPS9D1-AS1 KO tumor cells.

claim: Coculture with VPS9D1-AS1 knockout cells increased IFNAR1 expression in CD4+ T cells.
source: In vitro-primed T cells were cultured with HCT116 sgControl and sgVPS cell lines. Coculture with VPS9D1-AS1 KO cells increased IFNAR1 expression in CD8+ and CD4+ T cells (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B shows increased IFNAR1 on CD4+ T cells cocultured with VPS9D1-AS1 KO tumor cells.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 was positively associated with the expression levels of PD1 in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells of CRC patients.
source: However, VPS9D1-AS1 was found to be positively associated with the expression levels of PD1 of peripheral blood CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis of patient blood samples in Figure 5E shows higher PD1 levels on CD8+ T cells in VPS9D1-AS1 positive patients.

claim: Primed CD8+ T cells from OT-1 mice suppressed the proliferation of MC38-CTRL-OVA tumor cells.
source: Our models successfully demonstrated that primed CD8+ T cells from OT-1 mice suppressed the proliferation of MC38-CTRL-OVA and MC38-VPS9D1 OE-OVA tumor cells (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: T cell cytotoxicity assay in Figure 5F shows reduced tumor cell proliferation when cocultured with OT-1 CD8+ T cells.

claim: Primed CD8+ T cells from OT-1 mice suppressed the proliferation of MC38-VPS9D1 OE-OVA tumor cells.
source: Our models successfully demonstrated that primed CD8+ T cells from OT-1 mice suppressed the proliferation of MC38-CTRL-OVA and MC38-VPS9D1 OE-OVA tumor cells (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: T cell cytotoxicity assay in Figure 5F shows reduced tumor cell proliferation when cocultured with OT-1 CD8+ T cells.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing tumor cells inhibited CD8+ T cells from secreting IFN-γ.
source: FCM analysis showed that CD8+ T cells secreted more IFN-γ once they contacted tumor cells. However, VPS9D1-AS1 OE tumor cells inhibited CD8+ T cells from secreting IFN-γ.
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 5G shows reduced IFN-γ production by CD8+ T cells when cocultured with VPS9D1-AS1 OE tumor cells.

claim: Neutralizing antibodies against PD1 restored IFN-γ secretion by CD8+ T cells when cocultured with VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing tumor cells.
source: Furthermore, neutralizing antibodies against PD1 restored IFN-γ secretion by CD8+ T cells (Figure 5G).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 5G shows increased IFN-γ in CD8+ T cells when anti-PD1 antibody is added to coculture with VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 upregulates OAS1 by enhancing TGF-β signaling derived from cancer cells to protect themselves from T cell-mediated cytotoxicity through regulation of IFNAR1.
source: These data support the idea that VPS9D1-AS1 upregulates OAS1 by enhancing TGF-β signaling derived from cancer cells to protect themselves from T cell-mediated cytotoxicity through regulation of IFNAR1.
evidence: The collective data on VPS9D1-AS1 effects on TGF-β signaling, OAS1, IFNAR1, and T cell function support this mechanistic conclusion.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression promoted the expression of TGF-β in MC38 cells.
source: When we ectopically expressed full-length VPS9D1-AS1 in MC38 and CT26W cell lines (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), we observed an increase in the expression levels of TGF-β, TGFBR1, SMAD1, and STAT1 (Figure 6A).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 6A shows increased TGF-β protein in MC38 cells with VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression promoted the expression of TGFBR1 in MC38 cells.
source: When we ectopically expressed full-length VPS9D1-AS1 in MC38 and CT26W cell lines (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), we observed an increase in the expression levels of TGF-β, TGFBR1, SMAD1, and STAT1 (Figure 6A).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 6A shows increased TGFBR1 protein in MC38 cells with VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression promoted the expression of SMAD1 in MC38 cells.
source: When we ectopically expressed full-length VPS9D1-AS1 in MC38 and CT26W cell lines (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), we observed an increase in the expression levels of TGF-β, TGFBR1, SMAD1, and STAT1 (Figure 6A).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 6A shows increased SMAD1 protein in MC38 cells with VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression promoted the expression of STAT1 in MC38 cells.
source: When we ectopically expressed full-length VPS9D1-AS1 in MC38 and CT26W cell lines (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), we observed an increase in the expression levels of TGF-β, TGFBR1, SMAD1, and STAT1 (Figure 6A).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 6A shows increased STAT1 protein in MC38 cells with VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression.

claim: NR045849 overexpression did not increase the levels of TGF-β in MC38 cells.
source: NR045849 OE did not increase the levels of TGF-β in MC38 cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: Western blotting in Figure 6A shows no change in TGF-β protein in MC38 cells with NR045849 overexpression.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 shared similar biological functions in murine and human cells.
source: These findings indicated that VPS9D1-AS1 shared similar biological functions in murine and human cells.
evidence: The observation that human VPS9D1-AS1 increases TGF-β pathway proteins in mouse cells suggests conserved function.

claim: MC38 VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cells exhibited a higher speed of growth than control cells in vitro.
source: VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells exhibited a higher speed of growth than control cells in vitro (Figure 6B).
evidence: CCK8 assay in Figure 6B shows increased proliferation rate of MC38 VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: MC38 VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing cell-derived tumors grew faster than MC38 control cell-derived tumors in vivo.
source: MC38 VPS OE cell-derived tumors grew faster than MC38 CTRL cell-derived tumors (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D-F).
evidence: Tumor growth curves in Figure 6C show larger tumor volumes in mice injected with VPS9D1-AS1 OE cells.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression prevented CD4+ T cells from infiltrating into tumor tissue.
source: When allograft tumors were digested into single cells and analyzed by FCM, however, we found that VPS9D1-AS1 OE prevented CD4/8+ T cell from infiltrating into the tumor tissue (Figure 6E).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 6E shows lower percentages of CD4+ T cells in VPS9D1-AS1 OE tumors.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression prevented CD8+ T cells from infiltrating into tumor tissue.
source: When allograft tumors were digested into single cells and analyzed by FCM, however, we found that VPS9D1-AS1 OE prevented CD4/8+ T cell from infiltrating into the tumor tissue (Figure 6E).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 6E shows lower percentages of CD8+ T cells in VPS9D1-AS1 OE tumors.

claim: The levels of PD1 on CD8+ T cells were elevated in mice bearing MC38 VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing tumors.
source: The levels of PD1 on CD8+ T cells were elevated in mice bearing MC38 VPS OE tumors (Figure 6F), while CD44, CD107, CD62L, and CCR7 expression were not significantly different in either spleens or allografted tumor tissues (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 6F shows higher PD1 expression on CD8+ T cells in VPS9D1-AS1 OE tumors.

claim: CD44, CD107, CD62L, and CCR7 expression were not significantly different in spleens or allografted tumor tissues between control and VPS9D1-AS1 overexpressing groups.
source: The levels of PD1 on CD8+ T cells were elevated in mice bearing MC38 VPS OE tumors (Figure 6F), while CD44, CD107, CD62L, and CCR7 expression were not significantly different in either spleens or allografted tumor tissues (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1H shows no significant differences in these markers.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 regulated the pathway that controls the activation or differentiation of CD8+ T cells.
source: These results indicated that VPS9D1-AS1 regulated the pathway that controls the activation or differentiation of CD8+ T cells.
evidence: The selective effect on PD1 but not other T cell markers suggests VPS9D1-AS1 affects specific T cell differentiation pathways.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 was found to specifically express in intestinal epithelium of VPS Tg mice.
source: VPS9D1-AS1 was found to specifically express in intestinal epithelium of VPS Tg mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: RNA FISH in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B shows VPS9D1-AS1 expression in intestinal epithelium of transgenic mice.

claim: VPS Tg mice showed markedly higher intestinal tumor growth than WT mice after AOM/DSS treatment.
source: After AOM/DSS treatment, VPS Tg mice showed markedly higher intestinal tumor growth than WT mice (Figure 7B-D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Tumor images and volume measurements in Figure 7B-D show larger tumors in VPS Tg mice.

claim: VPS Tg mice had a shorter overall survival time than WT mice after AOM/DSS treatment.
source: The VPS Tg mice had a shorter OS time than the WT mice (Figure 7E).
evidence: Kaplan-Meier survival curve in Figure 7E shows reduced survival in VPS Tg mice.

claim: VPS Tg mice showed lower CD8+ T cell infiltration in AOM/DSS-induced tumors.
source: Interestingly, VPS Tg mice showed lower CD8+ T cell infiltration (Figure 7F-G).
evidence: Immunofluorescence staining in Figure 7F-G shows fewer CD8+ T cells in VPS Tg tumors.

claim: Ifnar1 levels in tumor tissues were increased in VPS Tg mice compared to WT mice.
source: However, Ifnar1 levels in tumor tissues were increased in VPS Tg mice (Figure 7H), indicating that VPS9D1-AS1 OE promoting Ifnar1 expression in tumor cells enhanced tumor growth.
evidence: IHC analysis in Figure 7H shows higher Ifnar1 levels in VPS Tg tumors.

claim: VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression promoting Ifnar1 expression in tumor cells enhanced tumor growth.
source: However, Ifnar1 levels in tumor tissues were increased in VPS Tg mice (Figure 7H), indicating that VPS9D1-AS1 OE promoting Ifnar1 expression in tumor cells enhanced tumor growth.
evidence: The correlation between VPS9D1-AS1 overexpression, increased Ifnar1, and enhanced tumor growth supports this conclusion.

claim: Transfection of ASOs targeting VPS9D1-AS1 impaired the proliferation of HCT116 cells in culture.
source: Transfection of ASOs targeting VPS9D1-AS1 impaired the proliferation of HCT116, SW480, and MC38 VPS OE cells in culture (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: CCK8 assay in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E shows reduced proliferation after ASO treatment.

claim: Transfection of ASOs targeting VPS9D1-AS1 impaired the proliferation of SW480 cells in culture.
source: Transfection of ASOs targeting VPS9D1-AS1 impaired the proliferation of HCT116, SW480, and MC38 VPS OE cells in culture (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: CCK8 assay in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E shows reduced proliferation after ASO treatment.

claim: Transfection of ASOs targeting VPS9D1-AS1 impaired the proliferation of MC38 VPS OE cells in culture.
source: Transfection of ASOs targeting VPS9D1-AS1 impaired the proliferation of HCT116, SW480, and MC38 VPS OE cells in culture (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: CCK8 assay in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E shows reduced proliferation after ASO treatment.

claim: ASO-VPS significantly inhibited tumor growth in BALB/c nude mice bearing HCT116 xenograft tumors.
source: We treated BALB/c nude mice bearing HCT116 xenograft tumors with intratumoral injection of ASO drugs and demonstrated that ASO-VPS significantly inhibited tumor growth in vivo (Figure 7I~J, Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
